label: Okta
note: Okta Customer / Workforce Identity. Guidance covers authenticators and phishing resistance, ThreatInsight and adaptive policy, token and session handling, and app client credentials.

questions.label: Authenticators
questions.text: Which authenticators can satisfy your app sign-in (authentication) policies? (select all that apply)

guidance.text: **Strong posture.** Passkeys (FIDO2 WebAuthn) are phishing-resistant. Turn on the 'Phishing resistant' requirement in the app sign-in policy so weaker factors cannot be used as a fallback.

**Strong posture.** Okta FastPass is phishing-resistant when the app sign-in policy strictly enforces phishing resistance (no fallback). Also require an existing phishing-resistant factor before enrolling new authenticators to protect the enrollment flow.

**Review.** Okta Verify push/TOTP (without FastPass) is not phishing-resistant and is exposed to adversary-in-the-middle and push-fatigue attacks. Enable number challenge and prefer Passkeys or FastPass for sensitive apps.

**Review.** SMS, voice, and email OTP are weak (SIM-swap, interception, toll fraud). Okta recommends replacing them with Passkeys or FastPass; keep only as a last-resort recovery factor with anti-toll-fraud protection.
**GAP.** Password-only sign-in. Require a second factor through an authentication policy and move toward phishing-resistant authenticators (Passkeys or FastPass).

**GAP.** No MFA. Enforce MFA with an app sign-in policy. The default 'Any two factors' policy is for testing only; replace it with a policy that requires phishing-resistant factors and uses device/risk context.

questions.label: ThreatInsight & adaptive policy
questions.text: Is Okta ThreatInsight enabled, and do authentication policies use risk/context (device assurance, network zones, behaviour)?

guidance.text: **GAP.** Enable ThreatInsight (Security > General) to block known-malicious IPs, and add risk/context conditions (device assurance, network zones, behaviour) to authentication policies so sign-ins step up on risk.
**Review.** ThreatInsight is log-only. Move to log-and-block for known-bad IPs once tuned, and add risk/context conditions to your sign-in policies.
**Good.** ThreatInsight is blocking and policies are risk-aware. Stream the System Log to your SIEM and alert on rate-limit, new-device, and impossible-travel signals.

questions.label: Tokens & sessions
questions.text: How are OIDC tokens and sessions configured for your apps?

options.label: Short-lived access tokens, refresh-token rotation, bounded sessions

guidance.text: **Review.** Shorten access-token lifetime, enable refresh-token rotation in the custom authorization server, and set global session idle/absolute limits proportionate to risk. Long-lived static tokens widen the account-takeover window.
**Review.** Confirm the authorization server's token lifetimes and refresh-token rotation, and set global session idle/absolute limits proportionate to the product's sensitivity.
**Good.** Short-lived tokens with refresh rotation and bounded sessions support reuse detection. Validate JWT signature (JWKS), issuer, audience, and expiry on every request.

questions.label: App client credentials
questions.text: How are OAuth client credentials handled for browser / native (public) apps?

options.label: Public app, Authorization Code + PKCE, no secret
Confidential app, secret kept server-side only
Client secret embedded in the SPA / native app

guidance.text: **GAP.** Public clients must not carry a secret. Use the Authorization Code flow with PKCE for SPA/native apps and keep any client secret server-side only.
**Good.** Public app with PKCE, or a confidential app whose secret stays server-side. Register exact (non-wildcard) redirect URIs and rotate any secrets.
